newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: The French 10-year bond future settled just off a new all-time high but volume was extremely thin and analysts were unsure the strong performance would last.
Dealers said that investors were displaying extreme caution in the face of a market that was at such levels.
"The fundamentals argue for a continuation of the rise but the level of the market means investors are asking themselves a lot of questions before committing themselves," said one dealer.
The March 10-year future settled at 131.46, up 18 points, after hitting a new historic high of 131.50 in earlier trading. But volume was a sparse 47,065 contracts.
Dealers said buying by domestic fund managers was responsible for pushing the notionnel to new highs. But many players were away on winter vacations coinciding with school holidays.
"All this means that 131.54/56 will not be an easy zone to break," said one dealer. "If we get through that level, it calls for more buying because the trend will be sustainable."
"But right now it's risky to buy contracts at these levels," he said. "It's better to look at options or calls in order to play a rise without being too exposed."
On the downside, 131.16 was seen as strong support.
On the cash market, the 6.50 OAT 2006 hit a new historic low of 5.45 with the spread over the comparable Bund stable at minus 16 basis points.
March and June PIBOR were flat while other expiries showed slight gains.

Analyst said the market would be looking to the U.S. for direction. Analysts said they believed the French market would not make any major advance from current levels ahead of the batch of U.S. data due on Friday, including producer prices, capacity utilisation and industrial production.

Some analysts said they believed the outlook for the French market hinged on the direction of the U.S. market but others believed a supportive European interest rate climate could allow the French bond market to advance still further.
Last week's data showing the total number of jobless in Germany hit a record 4.66 million people "as extremely favourable to the European bond market," Nordine Naam of BIP.
